issue.body:
Refs https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/3487

Resolves naming conflict with an action name "log" and `/some_controller/log`.
I think logging can be limited to the scope of the class where it was declared in (by including the LogTrait). It is easy enough to include the trait if needed.

body:
The `log()` and `set()` methods are not _new_. They have both been around since pre 1.x days.  Making `render()` protected could break userland components.

While I agree that many of the methods could be protected, they have historically been public. I'm not sure switching them really has much benefit to the end developer. Changing them does create more code they have to churn if/when applications upgrade to 3.0

@markstory I think we should prefer to not add more reserved action names, so +1 to not making cell a reserved word.

Using an underscore might be better, though I think that breaks some PSR. So I have no suggestions for a fix :(
We still use leading `_` for protected methods :)

The way "cells" work in CRUD is something like `$cell = (new IndexAction($this))->process();` 

Maybe we don't need a wrapper, but just simply pass in the controller to the cell, or whatever is needed :)

Some alternatives to cell() I can think of are:
- makeCell()
- getCell()
- buildCell()

I'm sure there are more, but those came to mind first. The original idea with `cell()` was that it followed the same convention as `element()` when used in `View`.
Was pre/postfixing actions ever an option?
@ndm2 It is an option for sure. Other frameworks frequently use `Action` as a method suffix.
please no I dont want to do `executeIndex()` and have an `indexSuccess.php` file anywhere other than at work :(
if you really want a cell() method, fix it in your route to map /:controller/:cell to Controller::myCell ? :P

@josegonzalez in general I can either see prefixes and suffixes everywhere or more reserved keywords, don't you agree?

Generally, reserved keywords are mostly bad to me, if they are document-able yet not documented (well). It is much worse then if they pass through hidden. In this case there is an error thrown through the method's visibility difference.

I can't comment for instance on the implications of making `render()` protected (is it really an issue for the future) - if it is only about upgrading, why not make the change now?

As for reserved keywords clashing with nice URLs via the controller space, @jippi routing suggestion is a good one.

Maybe there should be a chapter about reserved words (did not find any yet) as well as possible clashes and how to avoid them or work around them.

> Maybe there should be a chapter about reserved words.

It is generally only relevant in Shells and Controllers. Would better errors when overlays happen help? For example right now you get a MissingActionException. Perhaps we could have a more specific error for this situation?

@markstory You don't get that exception. You get the E_STRICT errors mentioned above + `Private Method in ArticlesController` exception. At least for "log" and "cell" and all non-action public methods declared in the controller.

Just a word of caution. With the increasing usage of traits we're going to have more and more method name conflict problems. Not only that, but code is harder to read and understand, it's happenning now to me with CakePHP3. Using object composition instead of traits would encapsulate functionality inside objects and less conflicts would happen. Code readability would be improved too since we're forced to split functionality in objects. Traits can be great for protopying, but I think they're not so beneficial in a framework. Composition over inheritance is a good design principle, traits are like multiple inheritance and can be easily abused.
